data.title: Project Coordinator - School of Medicine
data.description:
Overview

The mission of Tufts University School of Medicine Office of Continuing Education (OCE) is to foster and support continuing professional development and life-long learning for Tufts-affiliated physicians, nurses, and other health practitioners, as well as local, national, and international healthcare providers through high-quality, evidence-based continuing education (CE) activities. The ultimate goal is improved delivery of patient care and patient health outcomes. Tufts University School of Medicine OCE fulfills its mission by certifying/providing different types of continuing education activities (live meetings, online courses, Regularly Scheduled Series (RSS) at affiliated hospitals, etc.) to healthcare professionals. Tufts University School of Medicine OCE is accredited by The Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME) to provide credits to physicians, and The American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) to provide contact hours for nurses.

What You'll Do

Provides advanced support and coordination for Tufts School of Medicine OCE educational activities—including, but not limited to, RSS, live conferences, online activities, and enduring materials—to ensure they are planned, implemented, and documented in accordance with Tufts University School of Medicine OCE policies, national accreditation standards and criteria, documentation requirements, and established timelines, while providing exceptional customer service and maintaining organizational efficiency.

 

  • Serves as a main Regularly Scheduled Series (RSS) contact, providing the following support:
    • Reviewing annual RSS Planning Form submissions and communicating with RSS faculty/ administrators on missing or incomplete materials;
    • Leading RSS trainings for course directors and administrators;
    • Reviewing RSS session documentation and providing accurate feedback to RSS administrators/faculty;
    • Maintaining RSS timelines/deadlines, collecting required documentation, and tracking deliverables
    • Responding to inquiries from RSS faculty, administrators, and learners by providing detailed guidance on accreditation policies, procedures, and continuing education requirements
    • Managing end-of-year RSS reports and generating certificates
  • Organizes and maintains activity files/reports, accreditation files/reports, internal databases, and our online learning management system (eeds) for institutional and national accrediting body compliance and reporting.
  • Generates/distributes activity invoices; monitors electronic payments via internal system (TouchNet) to ensure timely receipt; and maintains accurate financial records in activity files.
  • Communicates with non-RSS course directors, planning committee members, faculty, participants, commercial supporters, exhibitors, and medical education companies, as necessary, to coordinate various aspects of continuing education requirements.
  • Co-leads the onboarding and training of new student workers and contributes to the onboarding of new Project Coordinators by sharing subject matter expertise, providing guidance, and supporting knowledge transfer to promote successful integration into the role.

What We're Looking For

Basic Requirements:
Knowledge and experience typically acquired by:
  • Associate's Degree
  • 3-5 years of related office experience
Preferred Qualifications:
  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Familiarity with CE standards, requirements, and policies of the ACCME, AMA, ANCC, and other health care organizations/accrediting bodies.
  • Familiarity with adult learning principles.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Access), Box and Adobe Acrobat PC.
  • Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to quickly learn new software applications, accreditation requirements, and organizational processes.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple concurrent educational activities while consistently meeting deadlines and multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong leadership skills, including the ability to take initiative, work independently, exercise sound judgment, and proactively solve problems.
  • Excellent presentation, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills, with the confidence to lead trainings, present accreditation requirements, and serve as a trusted resource for faculty, course directors, administrators, learners, and educational partners.
  • Demonstrates a commitment to continuous learning by proactively leveraging available resources and participating in professional development opportunities to expand knowledge, develop new skills, and enhance job performance.

Pay Range

Minimum $27.85, Midpoint $33.15, Maximum $38.50
 

Salary is based on related experience, expertise, and internal equity; generally, new hires can expect pay between the minimum and midpoint of the range.

data.title: Research Assistant - Neuroscience (Armbruster Lab)
data.description:
Overview

The Department of Neuroscience is a basic research department focusing on synaptic biology and glia biology. Dr. Armbruster within the Dulla Lab investigates how astrocytes modulate extracellular neurotransmitter and ionic concentrations around synapses in the physiological conditions and with a broad focus on neurological disease and epilepsy. We address this question in mouse models and apply electrophysiological and imaging approaches, together with mouse behavioral and in vivo electrophysiological studies.

What You'll Do

In collaboration with Principal Investigator, develop and modify techniques and protocols and provides input into research design focusing on distribution and function of astrocytic K+ channels to physiological functioning. Works independently performing a wide range of specialized techniques and experiments including stereotactic rodent surgeries, microscopy, and immunolabeling. Analyzes data, interprets results and assists in writing materials for publication and presentation. May supervise or provide work direction to others in the laboratory and helps manage laboratory operations. Will aid in ongoing lab maintenance, ordering, and more.

  • Conducts specialized laboratory experiments including stereotactic rodent surgeries, microscopy
  • Perform tissue preparation, immunohistochemical tissue labeling, and imaging
  • Develops research study design, techniques and protocols in collaboration with Principal Investigator
  • Reviews results and suggests modifications to experiments and protocols where necessary
  • Oversees collection and data entry of results
  • Analyzes and interprets data and drafts results of experiments
  • Writes summaries and material for presentation and publication

What We're Looking For

Basic Requirements:
Knowledge and experience typically acquired by:
  • Bachelor's Degree in science and 3-5 years of related laboratory experience or
  • Master's Degree and up to one year laboratory experience
  • 3-5 years related laboratory experience (with Bachelor's) or
  • Less than 1 related laboratory experience (with Master's)
  • Experience with rodent stereotaxic surgery
  • Highly organized with attention to detail/follow-up
  • Able to communicate with others effectively
Preferred Qualifications:
  • Master's Degree in science
  • Experience with immunohistochemical techniques
  • Experience with expansion microscopy
  • Experience with live-cell imaging
  • Experience with confocal microscopy
  • Data analysis experience
  • Knowledge of and experience with advanced laboratory techniques and procedures, data interpretation and statistical analysis

Pay Range

Minimum $50,500.00, Midpoint $63,200.00, Maximum $75,800.00
 

Salary is based on related experience, expertise, and internal equity; generally, new hires can expect pay between the minimum and midpoint of the range.
